## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR deletes `app/defaults.json`, but `app/startup.py` still reads that file, so `load_defaults()` will now raise on every call. That is a merge-blocking regression. There are also three Important defects: `is_valid_port` rejects the valid port 65535, `load_config` silently turns every failure into `{}`, and the `normalize_host` docstring promises `None` for empty input while the code returns `""`. The findings cover only the files in the pinned diff plus `app/startup.py`, which this review read because of the deletion.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — After this deletion, any call to `load_defaults()` raises `FileNotFoundError`, because the stale `app/startup.py:6` still runs `json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text())`. Nothing in the diff replaces the file or updates `startup.py`. Either keep `app/defaults.json`, or change `load_defaults()` to use another source (for example `load_config` with an explicit default of `{"timeout": 30}`) in this same PR. — Any startup path that calls `load_defaults()` crashes instead of getting the 30-second timeout default.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False`, but the docstring says "usable TCP port (1-65535)" and 65535 is a valid TCP port. The strict `p < 65535` leaves out the upper bound. Change it to `0 < p <= 65535` and add `assert is_valid_port(65535)` and `assert not is_valid_port(65536)` to `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound` or a companion test. The current test checks only 0, 1 and 8080, so it cannot catch this. — Services configured on port 65535 are wrongly rejected as invalid.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — If the config file is missing, unreadable, or contains malformed JSON (such as `{"timeout": 5,}`), `load_config` returns `{}`. That result is identical to a valid empty config. `except Exception: return {}` discards the `OSError` or `ValueError` without logging it and without telling the caller, and neither the docstring ("Load the JSON config at path.") nor a comment explains the fallback. Catch only `FileNotFoundError` if a missing file should mean "use defaults", document that in the docstring, and let parse errors propagate (or at least log them with the path). No test covers this fallback. — A typo in the config file makes the app run on defaults without any message, and operators have nothing to show why their settings were ignored.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — `normalize_host("")` returns `""`, but the docstring says it "returns None when h is empty". Line 37 is `return ""`. Make the docstring and code agree: either return `None` on line 37 or change the docstring to say it returns `""`. No test covers the empty-input branch. — A caller following the docstring with `if normalize_host(h) is None:` never sees the empty-host case and treats `""` as a valid host.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — No test exercises the trailing-dot branch (`if lowered.endswith("."): lowered = lowered[:-1]`). The only test, `test_normalize_host_lowercases`, passes `"Example.COM"`, which has no trailing dot. Add a case such as `assert normalize_host("Example.COM.") == "example.com"`. — A regression in stripping the fully-qualified dot, which the docstring names as core behavior, would pass the test suite.

## Strengths
- `test_parse_timeout_millis` checks the new `ms` branch with a concrete value (`"1500ms"` → `1.5`), so it fails if the division or suffix handling is wrong.
- `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound` checks both sides of the lower boundary (0 rejected, 1 accepted).
